=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:5163-5171 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The jobs jq filter (`try fromdateiso8601 catch null | select(. != null)`) silently drops a queued job whose `created_at` is missing or cannot be parsed. If that happens to every queued job in a run, `min // "none"` returns "none" and the run is treated like a concurrency-held run with no queued jobs.
  WHY: An unparseable jobs read then gives `outcome=short` (logged as a clear check) instead of the documented `outcome=read_failed` (docstring line 5055 and the linked issue), so no read-failed warning is emitted. It fails open and mirrors the existing run-level tolerance, so every flagging reviewer rated it NIT. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 judged it not a defect, because GitHub always returns an ISO-8601 created_at, and listed it as hardening only.
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:5113-5122, 5136, 5189-5190 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: When `_rgw_total > 100`, `_rgw_json` holds only the last page. `_rgw_candidate_count` comes from that page, so `runs_unread=$(( _rgw_candidate_count - _rgw_max_job_reads ))` is capped near 97 and undercounts the unread candidates. Example: total_count=250 gives runs_unread=47 when about 247 were unread.
  WHY: The outcome does not change. But the docstring (line 5048) and agents.d/10181-runner-wait-job-age.md promise the true unread count, and the AUTO_RELEASE_RUNNER_WAIT_CHECK and PROMOTE_CYCLE_RUNNER_WAIT_CHECK lines repeat the wrong value in exactly the deep-queue case the field exists for.
- agents.d/10037-release-gate-runner-wait.md:4 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: This fragment has not been folded yet and still documents the pre-#10181 contract: run-age measurement, `calls=<0|1|2>`, no jobs reads and no runs_unread. The new agents.d/10181-runner-wait-job-age.md targets the same "Workflow architecture" section with the new contract (`calls=<0..5>[ runs_unread=<n>]`, at most 3 jobs reads).
  WHY: Folding both fragments puts two conflicting output contracts for the same helper into agents.md, so later pipeline runs, parsers or reviewers may anchor on the obsolete calls bound. agents.d/* is in the plan grant, and §25 allows correcting existing fragment text.
- agents.d/10181-runner-wait-job-age.md | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The PR adds this new fragment but does not remove or update the existing fragment agents.d/10037-release-gate-runner-wait.md.
  WHY: Both fragments target section="Workflow architecture", so folding them puts contradictory descriptions of the helper's output contract into agents.md. This is the same root cause as the agents.d/10037 finding, filed against a different file.
- README.md:363 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The RELEASE_GATE_MAX_RUNNER_WAIT_MINUTES row still says "The runner wait is the age in minutes of the oldest live `queued` run of this repository", with a cost of 1-2 reads. The check now measures the oldest queued job's wait across the oldest 3 candidate runs, ignores concurrency-held runs and can make up to 5 reads. The env comment at .github/workflows/auto-release-stable.yml line 80 ("oldest live queued run") is stale in the same way.
  WHY: Nothing fails at runtime, but an operator tuning the limit or debugging a runner_wait_long skip is told the wrong thing about what is measured and what it costs. README.md and the workflow file are outside the plan grant's files_touched.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "The full test suite passes." (issue #10181, acceptance criterion 4)
  expected_change_site: PR validation covering tests/test_auto_release_stable.py and tests/test_promote_main_cycle.py
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: The PR Acceptance table marks all five new tests/test_auto_release_stable.py targets as "unmet" (test_runner_wait_held_run_without_jobs_dispatches, test_runner_wait_fresh_job_in_an_old_run_dispatches, test_runner_wait_job_waiting_past_the_limit_skips, test_runner_wait_jobs_read_failure_dispatches_with_a_warning, test_runner_wait_reads_at_most_three_runs_and_reports_runs_unread). The pre-push gate lists the whole file under "Inherited failures", with 30 inherited failing test files in total (e.g. tests/test_auto_release_stable.py, tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py, tests/test_review_autofix_review_pipeline_contract.py, tests/test_workflow_untrusted_input_contract.py), and ran only 99 selected test files. Criterion #4 is marked "unmet" with red-on-base status. Reviewers disagree on two points: z-ai_glm-5_3-flash says "Failures caused by this change: 0" and that neither of the PR's test files appears in the inherited failure list, while anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 reads the file-level failure as inherited from the merge-base. Severity also differs (MAJOR from minimax and luna, NIT from sonnet and glm).
- requirement: "The full test suite passes."
  expected_change_site: Overall PR CI status
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  EVIDENCE: The reported pre-push gate lists 30 inherited failing test files, so the goal "The full test suite passes" is unmet, which blocks the acceptance criteria. Rated MAJOR.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:release_gate_oldest_queued_wait, lines 5113-5122 and lines 5136 and 5189-5190 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When `_rgw_total > 100`, only the last page is counted, so runs_unread is at most 97 and undercounts the real unread candidates. Example: total_count=250 gives "queued_in_window=250 calls=5 runs_unread=47" when about 247 were unread.
  WHY: The outcome is unchanged, but the field under-reports how much of the check was skipped in the deep-queue case it exists for (the 2026-11-15 jam had 487 queued runs). It contradicts the docstring at line 5048 and agents.d/10181-runner-wait-job-age.md. Fix: when `_rgw_total > 100`, add (_rgw_total - candidates on the last page) to the count, or document the last-page-only behaviour (about 2 lines).
- agents.d/10037-release-gate-runner-wait.md:line 4 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The unfolded fragment still states the pre-#10181 contract (`calls=<0|1|2>`, no jobs reads, no runs_unread). The new agents.d/10181-runner-wait-job-age.md targets the same "Workflow architecture" section.
  WHY: The next fold puts two conflicting descriptions into agents.md, and a future parser could anchor "calls=" and accept only 0-2. Fix: change "calls=<0|1|2>" to "calls=<0..5>[ runs_unread=<n>]" and add "then reads the jobs of at most 3 candidate runs (issue #10181)" (1 line).
- README.md:line 363 (and .github/workflows/auto-release-stable.yml line 80) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Both still describe the run-age measurement ("oldest live `queued` run", one or two reads). The check now measures the oldest queued job across the oldest 3 candidate runs, ignores concurrency-held runs and can make up to 5 reads. Both files are outside the plan grant, so this is reported for visibility only.
  WHY: An operator tuning RELEASE_GATE_MAX_RUNNER_WAIT_MINUTES or reading a runner_wait_long skip is told the wrong thing.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: Acceptance criterion 4, "The full test suite passes."
  Expected change site: PR validation of tests/test_auto_release_stable.py (the five new test_runner_wait_* tests)
  Evidence of absence: The Acceptance table marks all five tests/test_auto_release_stable.py targets "unmet", and the pre-push gate lists the whole file under "Inherited failures". Only tests/test_promote_main_cycle.py::test_runner_wait_held_run_replay_runs_the_cycle is "met". The tests and the mock gh routing (lines 73-102) look consistent with the helper, which points to an inherited file-level failure.
  SEVERITY: NIT | ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- HARDENING: scripts/gh_helpers.sh jobs jq filter at lines 5163-5168: a queued job with an unparseable created_at is dropped silently instead of giving outcome=read_failed. Fix: replace "(try fromdateiso8601 catch null) | select(. != null)" with "fromdateiso8601" so the existing "|| true" plus the ^[0-9]+$ check at line 5172 yields read_failed. About 2 lines changed. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1. The reviewer states this is not a defect, because GitHub always returns ISO-8601 created_at.
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

  WHY: If all of a run's jobs have malformed timestamps, the run is treated as having no queued jobs instead of failing open with outcome=read_failed, which can hide data issues or API anomalies.

  WHY: An operator tuning the limit or debugging a runner_wait_long skip gets inaccurate information about how it is measured and what it costs.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:lines 5163-5169, the jobs jq filter `try fromdateiso8601 catch null | select(. != null)` | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A queued job with an unparseable `created_at` is dropped. If every queued job is dropped, `[... ] | min // "none"` gives "none", which the shell code treats as no queued jobs, so the result is `outcome=short`.
  WHY: The result fails open into `short` instead of the documented `outcome=read_failed`. The same pattern exists in the run-listing filter at lines 5117-5120, and this change extends it to a new endpoint.
- agents.d/10037-release-gate-runner-wait.md:line 4 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The unfolded #10037 fragment still documents `calls=<0|1|2>` and run-age semantics. agents.d/10181-runner-wait-job-age.md targets the same `## Workflow architecture` section and is folded after it by filename order.
  WHY: agents.d/ is in files_touched and §25 allows the correction, yet the fold will leave two contradictory statements in agents.md.
- README.md:line 363, the `RELEASE_GATE_MAX_RUNNER_WAIT_MINUTES` row in the Variables table | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The row still documents run-age behaviour and the old cost (1-2 reads), while the check now uses job age across 3 runs, ignores held runs and makes up to 5 reads.
  WHY: Operators get a stale description. README.md is not in the plan grant's files_touched.
